text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London finished modestly lower after holding in a tight range in late trading. May ended down $1.00 to close at $306.00 per tonne, while August gave up $0.70 to close at $305.00 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York ended lower across the board with front month May loosing 4 points to close at 10.88 cents/lb, while July shed 6 points to close at 10.61 cents/lb. The market was dull due to a dearth of fundamental news.
THAILAND - Sugar production up to March 17, 1997, reached 4.937 mn tonnes, tel quel (5.117 mn tonnes raw value), up from 4.881 mn tonnes (5.059 mn tonnes) produced the same period in 1995/96.

Industry sources said cane quality is far better than at the start of the crushing season and also the sugar yield has improved. However, commercial cane sugar remained with 11.62 per cent below last year's 12.03 per cent.

BRAZIL - Sugar output in February 1997 amounted to 459,200 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 547,900 tonnes. This brought cumulative production in the first ten months of 1996/97 (May/February) up to 14.436 mn tonnes against 13.451 mn tonnes in the like period the previous year.

Total production in 1995/96 amounted to 13.661 mn tonnes against 12.598 mn tonnes in 1994/95 and 10.112 mn tonnes in 1993/94. The sugar produced in February originates almost exclusively from the North/Northeast where the campaign is to finish in April. Alcohol production in May/February 1996/97 reached 14.150 bn litres, sharply up on last year's 12.524 bn litres.

Output in the North/Northeast so far amounted to 2.042 bn litres against 1.621 bn litres, while the Center/South accounted for 12.108 bn litres compared to 10.903 bn litres. Of the total produced so far in 1996/97 9.641 bn litres was hydrous alcohol (1995/96: 9.557 bn litres) and 4.509 bn litres anhydrous alcohol (2.966 bn litres).

HONG KONG - Sugar imports in January 1997 amounted to 32,883 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 20,197 tonnes. Total imports in calendar year 1996 reached 285,492 tonnes against 237,332 tonnes in 1995 and 208,640 tonnes in 1994.

Major countries of origin in January 1997 were South Korea with 21,143 tonnes whites against 11,810 tonnes and China with 2,947 tonnes compared to 1,604 tonnes. Sugar exports in January 1997 amounted to 6,385 tonnes compared to 4,099 tonnes in January 1996. Total exports in 1996 reached 18,533 tonnes against 67,970 tonnes in 1995.
The major country of destination in January 1997 was China with 4,883 tonnes whites against 2,797 tonnes in January 1996.
Libya is in the market to buy at least one cargo of white sugar. Further details were not immediately available.
Iran's Government Trading Corporation (GTC) bought 30,000 tonnes of raw sugar at $273.00 per tonne for shipment in May from a French trade house.
Bangladesh state-owned Sugar and Food Corporation has scheduled a buying tender on March 22 for 25,000 tonnes whites to be shipped in two equal installments by May 8 and May 15.
F.O. LICHT - Our first estimate of European sugar beet areas 1997 will be released on Thursday, March 20 at 14.00 hrs CET.
